Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

I must go phrase

also I have to go, I’ve got to go, we have to go now, I must be going, I must be off, I’m off

classical

Plaut. Am. 1.3.29: clam illūc redeundum est mihi (Lewis & Short s.v. illic)
Traupman 16: quīn nunc abeundum mihi est
Traupman 17: nōbīs nunc eundum est

Abeundum mihi est.

gerundive of necessity, impersonal, with the person in the dative; so nōbīs eundum est, we must go

I must go, I must be off

Literally “there must be going away by me”: the verb is impersonal and the person goes into the dative.

Other words

  • Tempus est mē abīre. — it’s time for me to go

    also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 1.99: tempus est jam hinc abīre mē (Lewis & Short s.v. tempus)

  • Abeō. — I’m off

    also used · classical · Plaut. Capt. prol. 67: abeō: valēte (Lewis & Short s.v. valeō)

    The plain present announces the leaving, often with valē.

Examples

  • Quīn nunc abeundum mihi est. Valē.

    Well, I must go now. Goodbye.Traupman 16

  • Nōbīs nunc eundum est.

    We have to go now.Traupman 17

  • tempus est jam hinc abīre mē

    it is time now for me to go henceCic. Tusc. 1.99 (Lewis & Short s.v. tempus)

See also must, goodbye, it’s time to …, where are you off to?.

SourcesLewis & Short: abeo · Lewis & Short: tempus

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 16–17, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
